title: sse: fix streaming chunking/framing for partial JSON + delimiter/token ordering (regression)
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: This change fixes a regression in the SSE streaming path that caused partial JSON payloads and delimiter ordering issues to produce invalid/ill-formed streamed JSON events in some low-latency cases. The regression was introduced when token-level flushes were made more aggressive to reduce latency; in certain interleavings the stream emitted token fragments and framing delimiters in an order that made incremental JSON assembly invalid for downstream consumers (OpenAI-compatible clients, some JS SSE parsers).

Motivation and root cause: We optimized the streaming runtime to flush on token boundaries for lower tail latency. However the flush/emit path did not maintain the invariant that framing delimiters (partial/finished object boundaries) are emitted before the next event's tokens when a single logical JSON object is emitted across multiple SSE data frames. In practice this led to sequences like: data: "{"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"{\"id\":"123\""}}"
 followed by the closing delimiter in a later frame, which broke some partial-JSON reassembly logic in client SDKs and the OpenAI-compatible layer.

What this PR does:
- Rework the SSE emitter to enforce an ordering invariant: framing/delimiter events (object/field boundaries and partial-json delimiters) are always emitted before tokens that belong to the following logical event.
- Add a lightweight boundary coalescer that merges token flushes that belong to the same logical JSON object when they are within the same dispatch window, preventing accidental mid-object delimiter emission. This keeps latency benefits but avoids malformed partial JSONs.
- Add end-to-end integration tests that exercise partial-JSON edge cases against the OpenAI-compatible SSE client harness (node/python).
- Add a regression unit test for token/event ordering and a fuzz test for random chunk splits.
- Fix a bug in the SSE framing code that omitted the separator when an event had no text delta but had metadata-only deltas (function/tool-calling cases).

Testing and CI: Initial CI run surfaced a failing integration test that reproduced the malformed-stream issue using the node SSE harness. After adjustments to the boundary coalescer the tests pass locally and in CI. Performance and latency were benchmarked in perf-canary; the median token latency impact is +1.2ms (acceptable) while 99th remains unchanged within noise.

Compatibility and rollout: No API surface changes. This is a server-side streaming stability fix and is safe to roll out. We will roll out to staging and then gradually to production using the existing canary policy.

Related: ENG-1423 (streaming stability), ENG-1589 (OpenAI compat bugs).

Ava Martinez: It failed on the first run due to a race in the harness startup. I added a small backoff/retry in the test harness and re-ran CI. Subsequent runs passed.

release_notes: Fixed SSE streaming framing bug that could produce malformed partial JSON events in rare low-latency interleavings. Improves compatibility with OpenAI-style SSE clients and fixes tool/function-calling partial payloads.
